purpose: Historical evidence; not a new-game runtime schema or balance specification.
method: Static parsing of top-level literal assignments and array_push. Comments excluded; no PHP executed. Last assignment wins. Empty PHP arrays represented as JSON lists until named keys are assigned. Original IDs/spelling preserved.

absolute_monarchy.pedia: This reform will establish an absolute monarchy, a regime where most of the power is vested in an single, hereditary Head of State. Since there is no independent judiciary, civil rights are inexistent.

junta.pedia: This reform will establish a military junta, a regime where most of the power is vested in an Head of State installed by the army. Since there is no independent judiciary, civil rights are inexistent.

authoritarian_republic.pedia: This reform will establish an authoritarian republic, a regime where the governement is regulated by a legal framework. However, while this kind of regime often pretend to exert power in the sole interest of the people (such as communist states), the people cannot actually choose its leaders in free and fair elections. A written constitution establishes the judiciary as a de jure independent branch.

constitutional_monarchy.pedia: This reform will establish a constitutional monarchy, a regime where most of the power is vested in an elected body while a hereditary Head of State has reserve powers. In this regime, conventions dictates that the real executive power is hold by the Head of Government picked by the Legislature and her or his cabinet. Conventions make the judiciary a de facto independent branch.

parlementary_democracy.pedia: This reform will establish a parliamentary democracy, a regime where most of the power is vested in an elected body. In this regime, the Head of State is usually a ceremonial figure and the executive power is in fact hold by the Head of Government picked by the Legislature and her or his cabinet. A written constitution insure that judiciary power is vested in an independent branch.

presidential_democracy.pedia: This reform will establish a presidential democracy, a regime that emphasizes separation of powers. In this regime, the elected Head of State is usually also the Head of Government and exerts the executive power. The legislative power is vested in an independently elected body. A written constitution insure that judiciary power is vested in an independent branch.

abolish_rights.description: Abolish civil rights and judicial review
abolish_rights.pedia: This reform will abolish civil rights and the power of courts to override mesures deemed anticonstitutional. Civil rights are beneficial to economic growth, but undermine counter-insuregency.

grant_rights.description: Instate judicial review to guarantee civil rights
grant_rights.pedia: This reform will create a judiciary branch with power to override mesures deemed anticonstitutional and then enshrine civil rights in a constitution. Civil rights are beneficial to economic growth, but undermine counter-insuregency.

grant_rights_conventions.description: Conventions regognize judicial review and guarantee civil rights

tax_cut.pedia: This reform aims to boost economy by converting surpluses into tax cuts.

half_income.description: Set taxes between balance and maximal revenue

max_income.pedia: This reform aims to increase taxes up to the highest tolerated level to increase government's revenues. The drawback is that high taxes hamper economic development.

private_welfare.pedia: This reform aims to offer higher quality services and promote dynamism by letting the forces of market compete for this sector. The drawback is that for-profit corporations will ask higher subsidies than state-run establishments. Hence, this mesure is well advised for laissez-faire economies where the government do not allocate a lot of ressources to public services.

mixed_welfare.description: Run public establishments side-by-side with private ones
mixed_welfare.pedia: This reform aims to provides lower cost state-run services allong premium private services. While this reform doesn't provides the same scale economies than a nationalization, it benefits from having some form of market competition.

nationalized_welfare.pedia: This reform aims to reduces costs by eliminating cuts taken by for-profit establishments and making scale economies. Usualy, funds saved are reinvested to increase welfare programs breadth and universality. The drawback is that quality of services will suffer from the lack of competition and closing this market will hamper dynamism.

privatization.pedia: This reform aims to create a free market economy by privatizing enterprises. Free market economies have higher potential than planed ones, but are more vulnerable to market trends and tends to increase inequality.

nationalization.pedia: This reform aims to create a planed economy by nationalizing means of production. Planed economies are more stable than free markets and facilitate distribution of wealth, but tends to stagnate.

severe_polution_standards.description: Enact the most severe polution standards

abolish_welfare.pedia: This reform will abolish existing welfare programs. Welfare programs are beneficial to the population, but their high cost usually forces the government to increase taxes which hamper economic development. This reform also repeals environment protection laws.

safety_net.pedia: This reform will create a comprehensive, balanced, set of welfare programs. Welfare programs are beneficial to the population, but their high cost usually forces the government to increase taxes which hamper economic development. This reform also enacts environment protection laws.

abolish_police.pedia: This reform will abolish existing law enforcement organizations such as police departments, forensic labs and national agencies in order to decrease spendings.

law_enforcement.pedia: This reform will create law enforcement organizations such as police departments, forensic labs and national agencies. These organizations use public funds to combat crime.

create_national_police.description: Create a national law enforcement agency

abolish_infratructure.pedia: This reform will abolish existing subsidies to infrastructure projects.

subside_infrastructure.description: Allocate funds to subside moderate infrastructure projects
subside_infrastructure.pedia: This reform will subside the realisation of the most critically needed public works.

extensive_subside_infrastructure.description: Allocate funds to subside extensive infrastructure projects
extensive_subside_infrastructure.pedia: This reform will subside the realisation of a large number of public works and other major infratructure projects.

surpluses.title: Cut taxes ?
surpluses.text: Since the nation has budgetary surpluses, you have room to cut taxes to stimulate the economy strengh and dynamism.

choices.desc: Use all the surplus to cut taxes
Use half the surplus to cut taxes

deficit.title: Fighting deficit
deficit.text: The budget is actually in deficit. In the long run, this situation can hypothecate financial health. Since taxes are set below the threshold, you could increase the rate.

choices.desc: Increase taxes just enough to cover deficit
Increase taxes at the point between balance and maximal income
Increase taxes as much as possible to maximize government revenues

rampant_crime.title: Criminality is rampant
rampant_crime.text: The current high crime level hurts the economy. Reforming law enforcement by funding local police departments, forensic labs and a national agency may be necessary to curb the problem.

choices.desc: Create police departments at local level
Create a national law enforcement agency
Implement a complete reform of law enforcement organizations

high_polution.title: High polution
high_polution.text: Environment is now a critical problem. Such a level of polution has a bad incidence over the health level of the population. While damaging for the economy, stricter environmental laws should be envisaged.

choices.desc: Enact strict polution standards.
Enact the most severe polution standards.

politic.note: The political system defines the way power is exerciced.

monarchy.desc: The power is concentrated in the hands of an an absolute ruler.

autho.desc: The formal power structure is controlled by a small elite.

democracy.desc: The population chooses its leaders in free and fair elections.

legal.note: An independent judiciary is a prerequisite if you want to guarantee civil rights. While authoritarian regimes are not typically committed to civil rights, you could devise an utopian regime where the unelected government respect the Rule of Law and where the population enjoy extensive freedoms. In game terms, freedom will stimulate your economy but will hamper your capacity to suppress unrest if you set the taxes over an acceptable threshold.

rule_by_law.desc: Government instances must act according to the law.

rule_of_law.desc: Government instances must act according to the law and respect the fundamental rights protected by the constitution.

economy.note: The economic system defines how production is allocated and how the wealth is redistributed. In this game, total laissez-faire is viable provided that taxes are low and population is healthy and educated, but remains vulnerable to bad events. Planned economies are usually initially successful since growth is more stable but tend to stagnate rapidly. Social democratic economies are somewhere between the two. To build the most successful economy, you will have to fine tune government intervention to adapt it to the evolving context.

total_laissez_faire.desc: Enterprises are owned by private interests. There is no welfare per se, only private charity. The duties of the government is limited strictly to defense and administration of justice.

laissez_faire.desc: Enterprises are owned by private interests. There is no welfare per se, only private charity. The duties of the government is limited to defense, public safety and administration of justice.

mixed.desc: Most enterprises are privately owned, but there is a robust social net thanks to public services provided by state-run facilities.

planned.desc: All means of production are nationalized. The State funds extensive welfare programs.

This reform aims to reduces costs by eliminating cuts taken by for-profit establishments and making scale economies. Usualy, funds saved are reinvested to increase welfare programs breadth and universality. The drawback is that quality of services will suffer from the lack of competition and closing this market will hamper dynamism.

This reform aims to create a free market economy by privatizing enterprises. Free market economies have higher potential than planed ones, but are more vulnerable to market trends and tends to increase inequality.
This reform aims to create a planed economy by nationalizing means of production. Planed economies are more stable than free markets and facilitate distribution of wealth, but tends to stagnate.
Enact the most severe polution standards

This reform will abolish existing welfare programs. Welfare programs are beneficial to the population, but their high cost usually forces the government to increase taxes which hamper economic development. This reform also repeals environment protection laws.

This reform will create a comprehensive, balanced, set of welfare programs. Welfare programs are beneficial to the population, but their high cost usually forces the government to increase taxes which hamper economic development. This reform also enacts environment protection laws.
This reform will abolish existing law enforcement organizations such as police departments, forensic labs and national agencies in order to decrease spendings.
This reform will create law enforcement organizations such as police departments, forensic labs and national agencies. These organizations use public funds to combat crime.
Create a national law enforcement agency
This reform will abolish existing subsidies to infrastructure projects.
Allocate funds to subside moderate infrastructure projects
This reform will subside the realisation of the most critically needed public works.
Allocate funds to subside extensive infrastructure projects
This reform will subside the realisation of a large number of public works and other major infratructure projects.

value.title: Cut taxes ?
value.text: Since the nation has budgetary surpluses, you have room to cut taxes to stimulate the economy strengh and dynamism.

choices.desc: Use all the surplus to cut taxes
Use half the surplus to cut taxes

value.title: Fighting deficit
value.text: The budget is actually in deficit. In the long run, this situation can hypothecate financial health. Since taxes are set below the threshold, you could increase the rate.

choices.desc: Increase taxes just enough to cover deficit
Increase taxes at the point between balance and maximal income
Increase taxes as much as possible to maximize government revenues

value.title: Criminality is rampant
value.text: The current high crime level hurts the economy. Reforming law enforcement by funding local police departments, forensic labs and a national agency may be necessary to curb the problem.

choices.desc: Create police departments at local level
Create a national law enforcement agency
Implement a complete reform of law enforcement organizations

value.title: High polution
value.text: Environment is now a critical problem. Such a level of polution has a bad incidence over the health level of the population. While damaging for the economy, stricter environmental laws should be envisaged.

choices.desc: Enact strict polution standards.
Enact the most severe polution standards.

source_assignments.value: The political system defines the way power is exerciced.
The power is concentrated in the hands of an an absolute ruler.
The formal power structure is controlled by a small elite.
The population chooses its leaders in free and fair elections.

An independent judiciary is a prerequisite if you want to guarantee civil rights. While authoritarian regimes are not typically committed to civil rights, you could devise an utopian regime where the unelected government respect the Rule of Law and where the population enjoy extensive freedoms. In game terms, freedom will stimulate your economy but will hamper your capacity to suppress unrest if you set the taxes over an acceptable threshold.
Government instances must act according to the law.
Government instances must act according to the law and respect the fundamental rights protected by the constitution.

The economic system defines how production is allocated and how the wealth is redistributed. In this game, total laissez-faire is viable provided that taxes are low and population is healthy and educated, but remains vulnerable to bad events. Planned economies are usually initially successful since growth is more stable but tend to stagnate rapidly. Social democratic economies are somewhere between the two. To build the most successful economy, you will have to fine tune government intervention to adapt it to the evolving context.
Enterprises are owned by private interests. There is no welfare per se, only private charity. The duties of the government is limited strictly to defense and administration of justice.
Enterprises are owned by private interests. There is no welfare per se, only private charity. The duties of the government is limited to defense, public safety and administration of justice.
Most enterprises are privately owned, but there is a robust social net thanks to public services provided by state-run facilities.
All means of production are nationalized. The State funds extensive welfare programs.
